messages.subject: Contribution to "Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools"
parts:
On Wednesday, March 9, 2016, Aaditya Jamuar <aadity...@gmail.com> wrote:

I am Aaditya Jamuar , Second Year Undergrad (Bachelor of Engineering- Information Technology) at Manipal Institute of Technology, India. I am interested to work in the field of Text Mining, NLP and Machine Learning and would like to contribute to the project " Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools" under GSOC 2016. 

I have solved the test cases provided on the project idea page .

Link : https://github.com/AadityaJ/test_itmr

Further, I would like to inform that I have good knowledge of programming and text processing in R.

I have previously made a shinyapp on wordcloud in R ( https://aadityaj.shinyapps.io/R-Worcloud/ ,  https://github.com/AadityaJ/Shiny-Wordcloud) . Beside this I have created a CAGRCalculator (https://aadityaj.shinyapps.io/CAGRCalc/)  

Aaditya, please share your thoughts on https://github.com/tomayac/wikipedia-tools-for-google-spreadsheets

Would you please also share your thoughts on  http://www.danielschlegel.org/pubs/MEDINFO15.pdf

As well as these? http://disaster-monitor.herokuapp.com
-- source code:
http://github.com/tomayac/postdoc/tree/master/demos/disaster-monitor
 -- papers: http://ceur-ws.org/Vol-1268/paper15.pdf and http://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.06329v1.pdf etc.
 -- slides:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1b563mkeP91PMWJ6B_Fy3DdKK-SjM06gPVNu2s1uAxBk/edit#slide=id.i0

I've mentored http://pronunciationeval.blogspot.com
which produced http://www.aclweb.org/anthology/W12-5808
This year I have been mentoring https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T89416

I do not know whether I will be invited to co-mentor for R this year, because this is a negative for me:

and also used R for backtesting of an automated trading algorithm . 

So, please share your thoughts on Thomas Philippon's findings as reported in http://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/business/2014/12/16/a-black-hole-for-our-best-and-brightest/

Documentation for both can be seen on my rpubs page : https://rpubs.com/AadityaJ/ 

 Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: Contribution to "Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools"
parts:
Aaditya,

Thanks for taking a look at those systems.

You would need to convince the lead mentor to put his email address in
the task description and ask Brian for an invitation to mentor.

I do not hold that you have worked on automatic programmed trading
against you, but I had hoped you would please share an opinion on the
finding that the U.S. finance sector is $300 billion per year, or 20%
too large relative to the size expected to maximize economic growth?

Best regards,
Jim


On Thu, Mar 10, 2016 at 8:05 AM, Aaditya Jamuar <aadity...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi James
>
> Thanks for the reply !
> I saw the github link to the "Wikipedia Tools for Google Spreadsheets" and i
> found it to be really nice and handy .
> The paper you send "Automatically Expanding the Synonym Set of SNOMED CT
> using Wikipedia" (http://www.danielschlegel.org/pubs/MEDINFO15.pdf) was
> really informative and made me understand the reasons for why use of simple
> directed graphs might be erroneous when trying to understand synonyms using
> wikipedia and so I support that using a more collection based approach for
> SNOMED CT enhancement would be better.Also I found the methodology of using
> a table to form a relation between SNOMED CT Semantic Type and Wikipedia
> Categories to be really thought provoking as to something which can be used
> in other fields of sciences too where "terminologies" play an important
> part.
> Beside I too have had experience with Web scrapping using python where I
> used it to find the interests of my teacher and map it using beautifulsoup .
>
> I also found the live disasterapp (http://disaster-monitor.herokuapp.com/)
> to be really useful.I was wondering for maybe there could be a memoize
> function to go with it so that the app can not only track disaster starting
> from that time that user enters the site but rather of a previous time
> period as well and storing it as a table (something like :
> http://quakes.globalincidentmap.com/ ) .
>
> Regarding your observation on my work on ’mean reversion in R(Algorithmic
> Trading Backtesting) . Bit on background -I started learning R during my
> first semester itself through MOOC by John Hopkins University and I enjoyed
> handling large data set of plenty of csv files. I also observed phenomena of
> variation in data around some trending mean. These led me to modeling this
> phenomenon that I later came to know as 'mean reversion'. I goggled ‘Mean
> reversion in R’ and that gave lots of link on mean reversion used in equity
> and also I found that there were lots of easily available data in India to
> code this mean reversion tendencies in data of related streams. So that
> project was to improve my ability to handle large data and coding ability in
> R.
>
> My interest lies primarily in basic research on data analysis , machine
> learning and natural language processing that can bring positive change to
> human productivity. And I agree completely with this article of Washington
> Post. In fact I had read a document that gives very convincing talk on how
> financial sector is detrimental to productivity growth. And being technology
> person first, my basic drive is to improve quality of human life with real
> productivity gains.
>
>
> I also saw project on "Automatic Pronunciation Evaluation And
> Mispronunciation Detection Using CMUSphinx" (
> http://www.aclweb.org/anthology/W12-5808) and
>
> (http://pronunciationeval.blogspot.in/) .
>
> I found the tool to be really insightful. I have a query whether nearest
> neighbors
> algorithm(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-nearest_neighbors_algorithm) along
> with the concept of Euclidean
> distances(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance) can be used to
> detect and evaluate the same .
>
>
> Thanks once again for your early reply. I also request you to provide me
> with feedback and suggestions about how i can start working early on this
> project on "Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools" .
>
>
> Aaditya

>
>
